subproblem.title: Hⁿ scaling law for the dilation η_{x,r}: measurable embedding and measure preservation
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, x ∈ ℝ^P, r > 0 and η(y) := r⁻¹(y − x). Then η : ℝ^P → ℝ^P is a measurable embedding, and η is measure preserving from c·Hⁿ to Hⁿ, where Hⁿ = μHE[n] and c = ENNReal.ofReal((rⁿ)⁻¹); equivalently η_*(c·Hⁿ) = Hⁿ, i.e. Hⁿ(η⁻¹(B)) = rⁿ·Hⁿ(B) for every Borel B.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (x : Eucl P) (r : ℝ), 0 < r → MeasurableEmbedding (fun y : Eucl P => r⁻¹ • (y - x)) ∧ MeasurePreserving (fun y : Eucl P => r⁻¹ • (y - x)) (ENNReal.ofReal ((r ^ n)⁻¹) • (μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl P))) (μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl P))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Step 6 (change of variables) of the parent proof, isolated as a lemma. Conventions: ℝ^P := Eucl P (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin P)); Hⁿ := μHE[n]; η(y) := r⁻¹ • (y − x); c := ENNReal.ofReal((rⁿ)⁻¹).
1. η is a homeomorphism of ℝ^P. It is the composite e of the translation y ↦ y + (−x) (Homeomorph.addRight (−x)) and the dilation z ↦ r⁻¹ • z (Homeomorph.smulOfNeZero r⁻¹, valid because r⁻¹ ≠ 0). Indeed e(y) = r⁻¹ • (y + −x) = r⁻¹ • (y − x) = η(y) (sub_eq_add_neg), so ⇑e = η.
2. Measurable embedding. A homeomorphism between Borel spaces is a measurable embedding (Homeomorph.measurableEmbedding). By step 1, η is a measurable embedding; in particular it is measurable and injective. This is the first conjunct.
3. Preimages. For every B ⊆ ℝ^P, η⁻¹(B) = (z ↦ x + z) '' ((z ↦ r • z) '' B).
   (i) If η(y) ∈ B, put b := r⁻¹ • (y − x) ∈ B. Then x + r • b = x + r • r⁻¹ • (y − x) = x + (y − x) = y (smul_inv_smul₀ with r ≠ 0, add_sub_cancel).
   (ii) Conversely, η(x + r • b) = r⁻¹ • ((x + r • b) − x) = r⁻¹ • r • b = b ∈ B (add_sub_cancel_left, inv_smul_smul₀).
4. Scaling of Hⁿ, valid for every set B ⊆ ℝ^P.
   (i) Translation z ↦ x + z is an isometry (isometry_add_left x), so Hⁿ(x + S) = Hⁿ(S) for every S (Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image).
   (ii) (z ↦ r • z) '' B = r • B (Set.image_smul). Hence Hⁿ(r • B) = ‖r‖₊ⁿ • Hⁿ(B) (Measure.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_smul₀, since r ≠ 0).
   (iii) Combining (i), (ii) and step 3, Hⁿ(η⁻¹(B)) = ‖r‖₊ⁿ · Hⁿ(B).
5. Constant. In ℝ≥0∞, c · (‖r‖₊ⁿ : ℝ≥0∞) = 1. Since r > 0, ‖r‖ = r, so (‖r‖₊ⁿ : ℝ≥0∞) = ENNReal.ofReal(rⁿ) (ENNReal.ofReal_coe_nnreal, NNReal.coe_pow, coe_nnnorm, Real.norm_of_nonneg). As (rⁿ)⁻¹ ≥ 0, ENNReal.ofReal_mul gives c · ENNReal.ofReal(rⁿ) = ENNReal.ofReal((rⁿ)⁻¹ · rⁿ) = ENNReal.ofReal 1 = 1, because rⁿ ≠ 0 (inv_mul_cancel₀).
6. Measure preservation. η is measurable by step 2. For every measurable B, (η_*(c·Hⁿ))(B) = (c·Hⁿ)(η⁻¹(B)) = c · Hⁿ(η⁻¹(B)) (Measure.map_apply, Measure.smul_apply). By step 4(iii) this is c · ‖r‖₊ⁿ · Hⁿ(B), and by step 5 it equals Hⁿ(B). Two measures that agree on all measurable sets are equal (Measure.ext), so η_*(c·Hⁿ) = Hⁿ. Thus MeasurePreserving η (c·Hⁿ) Hⁿ, the second conjunct. ∎
proof_key_steps: η = (translation by −x) followed by (dilation by r⁻¹) is a homeomorphism, hence a measurable embedding (Homeomorph.measurableEmbedding).
Hⁿ(x + r·B) = ‖r‖₊ⁿHⁿ(B) by translation invariance (Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image) and Measure.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_smul₀.
ENNReal.ofReal((rⁿ)⁻¹)·‖r‖₊ⁿ = 1 for r > 0, so η_*(c·Hⁿ)(B) = Hⁿ(B) for measurable B; conclude by Measure.ext.

audit.reason: The prose and exact type include all parameters and r > 0. The homeomorphism gives the measurable embedding; the preimage identity, translation invariance, and Hausdorff scaling give the stated measure-preserving direction and constant. Positivity correctly justifies invertibility and scalar cancellation. The proof is complete and independent of the parent and other children.
